caption_en:
This is utopia: a perfect 100 on Freedom House's scale. Israel is at 73.

So what's in the gap? Plenty.
• Corruption: former prime minister Ehud Olmert went to prison for bribery in 2016. Benjamin Netanyahu has been on trial since 2020 for bribery, fraud and breach of trust; he denies the charges. Transparency International: 62/100, 35th of 182 (2025).
• Prices: the 4th highest price level of the 38 OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) countries (OECD Economic Survey of Israel, 2025).
• Poverty: 20.7% of Israelis are poor, and child poverty is the 2nd highest in the OECD (National Insurance Institute, 2024 data).
• Press freedom: 116th of 180 (Reporters Without Borders, 2026). Qatar (75th) and Lebanon (115th) rank higher.
• Arab towns: a record 252 Arab citizens murdered in 2025 (Abraham Initiatives).

Now zoom out. Same scale, Freedom House 2026:
🇮🇱 Israel 73
🇱🇧 Lebanon 41
🇯🇴 Jordan 34
🇪🇬 Egypt 18
🇦🇪 UAE 18
🇸🇾 Syria 10
🇮🇷 Iran 10
🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia 9
Distance to utopia (100 minus the score): Israel 27, the neighbours 59 to 91. Every one of them is at least twice as far.

One honest catch: on corruption, the UAE scores cleaner than Israel (69 vs 62, Transparency International 2025).

We're not perfect. We know it. But on freedom, we're closer to utopia than anyone around us.

caption_he:
זו אוטופיה: 100 מתוך 100 במדד של Freedom House. ישראל ב־73.
מה יש בפער? שחיתות (ראש ממשלה לשעבר ישב בכלא, ונתניהו עומד לדין ומכחיש), יוקר מחיה, עוני, חופש עיתונות (מקום 116 מתוך 180), ושיא של 252 נרצחים בחברה הערבית ב־2025.
עכשיו תעשו זום אאוט: לבנון 41, ירדן 34, מצרים ואיחוד האמירויות 18, סוריה ואיראן 10, סעודיה 9. כל השכנות רחוקות מהאוטופיה לפחות פי שניים.
ובכנות: במדד השחיתות איחוד האמירויות מקבלת ציון טוב יותר משלנו.
אנחנו לא מושלמים. אנחנו יודעים. אבל בחופש, אנחנו הכי קרובים לאוטופיה באזור.

lines.line: This is utopia. Israel is here.
Seventy-three out of a hundred on Freedom House's scale.
Corruption. A former prime minister went to prison.
Netanyahu is on trial for bribery, fraud and breach of trust. He denies the charges.
Prices? Among the highest in the developed world.
Press freedom? A hundred and sixteenth out of a hundred and eighty.
Arab towns? A record two hundred fifty-two murders last year.
That's the gap. Now zoom out.
Lebanon, forty-one. Jordan, thirty-four. Egypt and the Emirates, eighteen. Syria and Iran, ten. Saudi Arabia, nine.
Every neighbour is at least twice as far from utopia.
One honest catch: on corruption, the Emirates score cleaner than us.
We're not perfect. We know it.
But on freedom, we're closer to utopia than anyone around us.
